hook: What an *API* actually is, explained without the jargon

points.title: A menu for software
points.body: An API lists what a program can do for you, and how to ask.

points.title: You send a request
points.body: Your app asks for something specific, like a user's profile or today's orders.

points.title: You get a response
points.body: The other system replies with data, usually as JSON, or an error explaining why.

caption:

Request in, response out. That is the whole idea.

hook: Over 16,000 *Supabase* databases have publicly readable tables

points.title: AI tools create tables with RLS off
points.body: The dashboard turns RLS on by default. Raw SQL migrations, common in AI tools, don't.

visual.title: migration.sql
visual.code:
-- written by an AI tool
create table public.orders (
  id uuid primary key,
  user_id uuid,
  email text
);
-- RLS is off unless you enable it

points.title: Turn RLS on for every table
points.body: One line per table. With RLS on and no policy, nobody gets rows.

visual.title: enable_rls.sql
visual.code:
alter table public.orders
  enable row level security;

points.title: Add a policy matching rows to users
points.body: Each user should read only their own rows. Never use true for anon.

visual.title: policy.sql
visual.code:
create policy "Own rows only"
on public.orders for select
to authenticated
using ( (select auth.uid()) = user_id );

5. Ask Claude to query your tables in plain English.

hook: Is storing your *login token* in localStorage safe?

points.title: Feels secure
points.body: Just your own code touching it

points.title: Any script reads it
points.body: One xss bug leaks everything

points.title: Use httpOnly cookies
points.body: JavaScript cannot read those cookies

visual.title: server.js

dm_guide: Skip localStorage for auth tokens, any XSS bug can read it instantly. Use an httpOnly cookie instead. Server side, set it like this: Set-Cookie: session=abc123; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Path=/. That header blocks JavaScript from ever touching the cookie. Pair it with a short expiry and refresh token rotation, and keep SameSite set to Strict or Lax to help with CSRF too. Docs: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTTP/Cookies and https://owasp.org/www-community/HttpOnly
caption:
localStorage vs httpOnly cookies for auth tokens
One XSS bug can leak everything sitting in localStorage
Where do you store your tokens? 👇
voiceover: [urgent] Quick question, is your login token sitting in localStorage?
[knowing] It looks harmless since nothing else seems to touch it.
[serious, fast] But one xss bug lets any script read it.
[confident and fast] Httponly cookies fix that, javascript simply cannot touch them.
